title: Cross-region degradation simulation and graceful cutover checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: build a repeatable simulation harness and an operational checklist that validates warm-standby readiness and enables a graceful cutover when a primary region degrades. The goal is to reduce failed rollovers, avoid capacity thrashing, and ensure application-level SLOs are preserved during cross-region failovers. This ticket scopes the simulation scenarios, the acceptance checks for a warm standby (health, KV-cache priming, model-variant compatibility), and the automated checklist used by the failover orchestrator to gate activation of standby pools.
acceptance_criteria: A simulation harness can inject three degradation modes (increased p99 latency, partial instance drain, and synthetic packet loss) against a staging multi-region topology

Warm-standby readiness gate implements the following checks and returns pass/fail within 60s: service liveness, prefix/KV cache hit rate >= 70% for representative prompt set, model-variant tokenization/embedding compatibility verified, and steady-state p95 latency below 1.5x primary baseline
Failover orchestrator uses the readiness gate to decide activation; automated cutover script performs canary traffic shift (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with rollback on metric regressions
Simulation runs are recorded and surfaced in a dashboard with run metadata, failing check traces, and guidance for remediation
Runbook checklist created and reviewed by SRE, Runtime, and Product; playbook includes post-cutover validation steps and rollback triggers
tasks: Design simulation harness (scenarios + traffic generator) and infra requirements
Implement readiness gate API (health, cache primer, model compatibility probe, latency probe)
Integrate readiness gate into regional failover controller with canary stages
Create Grafana dashboard and logging for simulation results and readiness gate traces
Author runbook, including escalation steps, expected time windows, and rollback criteria
E2E test: run simulation against staging, validate canary behavior, and record results
progress_updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket opened by Aisha. Initial scope drafted; blockers: need a stable staging topology that mirrors prod routing policies.
2026-03-03: Spike completed for latency-injection in staging using Toxiproxy. Confirmed ability to introduce p99 latency shifts and instance-level drains.
2026-03-05: Readiness gate prototype (health + basic latency probe) implemented. KV cache primer sketch reviewed by Runtime team.

2026-03-08: Design review with SRE and Product. Agreed on canary percentages (5 / 25 / 100) and a 10-minute observation window per stage. Action: add automated rollback on token-error rate > 0.5% or p95 increase > 2x baseline.
2026-03-10: Started dashboard and logging plumbing. Assigned Marco to complete integration with orchestrator and finalize runbook
decision_log: Use three canonical degradation modes rather than an exhaustive fault matrix to keep simulation runs tractable
Canary increments standardized to 5/25/100 after discussion with Product — balances detection speed with blast radius
KV cache primer will use a representative set of 500 prompt prefixes derived from production traces; sampling window agreed to be 24h
Failover controller will prefer same-tier standby region when capacity allows; cross-tier fallback requires explicit operator approval
test_plan: Scenario A: Primary region p99 latency doubles for 5 minutes -> orchestrator should run readiness gate, fail checks, and shift canary traffic to standby
Scenario B: 30% of model-serving instances in primary drain unexpectedly -> readiness gate should detect capacity mismatch and trigger controlled canary after capacity reservation verification
Scenario C: Partial network partition causing 5% packet loss to primary -> verify cache primer still achieves >=70% prefix hits within 90s or else abort cutover
Chaos run: combine latency + instance drains in stochastic patterns, verify dashboard captures root cause traces and that automated rollback triggers when SLO violations observed
telemetry_changes: Emit readiness_gate.detail.{health,cache,model_compat,latency} as tags on evaluation events
Add simulation.run_id and scenario labels to traces and logs
Create composite alert: readiness_gate_failure_rate > 0.5% over 15m during cutover => P0 incident
rollout_plan: 1) Merge readiness gate code to staging runtime; 2) Run three full simulation scenarios in staging and record results; 3) Iterate on primer size if cache hit < 70%; 4) Deploy controller integration to canary cluster; 5) Run operator-led cutover dry-run; 6) Schedule limited production window with stakeholder signoff
rollback_plan: Abort cutover and revert traffic to primary if any canary stage shows: token error rate increase > 0.5% OR p95 latency > 2x baseline
If controller fails to revert, activate manual routing via network-layer rewrite and notify on-call SRE
Post-mortem: capture run_id, attach traces, and run remediation checklist
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cache primer overfits to staging prefixes and fails in prod. Mitigation: use production-sampled prefixes and validate primer on a small prod shadow pool before full run
Risk: Automated rollback erroneously triggers due to noisy metrics. Mitigation: require two metric conditions or corroborating error logs before automatic rollback
Risk: Cross-tier activation causes higher cost and reduced performance. Mitigation: prefer same-tier standby, send operator approval prompt for cross-tier fallback
notes: This ticket focuses on the operator experience and automated gating logic rather than hardware-level scheduling. Follow-up tickets will cover kernel scheduling adjustments and autoscaler tuning if simulations indicate capacity shortfalls. Coordinate with ENG-81234 for readiness API contract and ENG-70321 for playbook alignment.
